newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds leads sector down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds leads sector down on profit-taking.

text.p: UK bank shares extended this week's sharp decline and were among the biggest losers in the FTSE 100 index on Thursday amid growing perceptions that interest rates are headed higher, dealers and analysts said.
At 1032 GMT, shares in Lloyds TSB Group were down 19p to 480. Shares in Abbey National Plc skidded 12-1/2p to 720, while shares in Barclays Plc stumbled 26-1/2p to 1050.
Shares in Standard Chartered Plc lost 19-1/2p to 829 and shares in National Westminster Bank Plc lost 11-1/2p to 692.
Shares in Bank of Scotland fell 13-1/2p to 326 and shares in Royal Bank of Scotland slipped 8p to 543.
Shares in HSBC Holdings, under the additional weight of a 1.4 percent drop in the Hong Kong stock market, sank 32p to 1482-1/2.
Bank shares, which have outpaced gains in the broad market for six months, have been under all week on worries about interest rates, they said.
"It's a sector where there are profits to be taken, and it's very interest-rate sensitive" said one dealer.
But analysts said interest rates would have to rise by one to 1.5 percent before banks would feel the pinch.
Separately, one analyst noted concerns that banks' margins would be squeezed as they compete for deposits with building societies, due to convert to bank status later this year.
"They'll have to pay more if they want to maintain their deposit base," the analyst said.
Yet he said he doesn't believe the bull market for banks is over.
"This is a good opportunity to take profits given the interest rate uncertainty and the upcoming election. But the fundamentals still look good," he added.
